products.name: Say Good Night to Insomnia: The Six-Week, Drug-Free Program Developed At Harvard Medical School

reviews.content: The information presented is clear and to the point; each chapter builds upon information previously presented without being redundant. Tools for application are easy to use, with step-by-step instruction in how to apply concepts and use the recommended journaling for tracking of progress. Problem solving concepts are easily understood, research based and well referenced for both the casual and professional reader. Utilization is simple, and the book may be read in sections as the ideas are implemented, or in full before applying techniques. The book is useful for the professional looking for concepts to help with clients, as well as an easily used tool for use by the reader.
reviews.title: Concise, on topic, research supported/referenced.

groupingData.productName: Say Good Night to Insomnia: The 6-Week Solution

reviews.content:
My doctor recommended this book for insomnia. I am embarrassed my doctor has any regard for this book. 
There is a lot of misinformation in this book. The author classifies Ambien as a benzodiazpine. It's absolutely not. 
The author seems to be against medication in general. It's really odd.
This book may be helpful for people who have insomnia due to situational or transient stress/ depression. But I deal with depression, GAD, panic disorder, ASD and ADHD. All of which are being undertreated. 
This book likely won't work if you have complex mental health or physical health issues that could contribute to your inability to sleep.
reviews.title: Terrible Book Full of Misinformation
